title: Canonical-form writer missed two Health_Meter fields (in_breach, healthy_streak) — struct/writer pairs must stay complete
evidence:
+	h := &state.health
+	w_i32(&w, h.meter_pct)
+	w_i32(&w, h.grace_ticks_left)
+	w_bool(&w, h.in_grace)
+	w_bool(&w, h.won)
+	w_bool(&w, h.lost)
+	w_u64(&w, h.surge_delivered)
+	w_u64(&w, h.surge_dropped)
+	w_bool(&w, h.prev_in_surge)
detail: ODN-11/§10.2 make this writer the T1 determinism contract; its header claims it covers ALL sim state. Health_Meter's hysteresis band state and refill streak are absent — exactly the omission class the Godot r1 fingerprint lesson was about.
recommended_fix: Serialize in_breach and healthy_streak; consider a per-struct checklist so future fields pair with writer lines.

title: App_Mode (the ODN-13 app FSM) is declared inside the pure core package
evidence: +App_Mode :: enum u8 { Boot, Menu, Run, Paused, Game_Over }
detail: Boot/Menu/Run/Paused/Game_Over is the App-struct mode machine (ODN-13, app layer). Declaring it in core blurs the ODN-1 layer line the whole determinism story rests on; nothing in this core diff references it.
recommended_fix: Move App_Mode to the app/run package.

title: snapshot.odin replaces the ODN-1 double-buffered SOA memcpy with a single live computed projection
evidence:
+// PROTO renders at sim rate (the Godot reference's cadence — its vis-dist
+// smoothness is carried as vis_q8), so a single live snapshot rewritten per
+// tick (and topology-only on edit fast-path) replaces the ping-pong pair.
detail: The canon pins snapshot = memcpy into ping-pong slots with view-side lerp. The code builds derived Snap_* structs in one live buffer — a deliberate, commented deviation, but the spec and code now describe two different snapshot architectures.
recommended_fix: Either rule the deviation (amend ODN-1 note) or implement the ping-pong memcpy.

title: pick_dst allocates per-spawn dynamic arrays from context.allocator inside the hot spawn loop
evidence:
+	cand: [dynamic]u32
+	cand_w: [dynamic]i32
+	defer delete(cand)
+	defer delete(cand_w)
detail: During step, context.allocator is the run arena, where delete is a near-no-op — the arena grows per spawn for the whole run. The same file's Flow_State comment advertises 'persistent — no per-tick allocator churn' scratch (sc_*), which this proc doesn't use.
recommended_fix: Reuse the persistent sc_* scratch buffers for the filtered sink list.

title: Comment names 'Run_State.economy' as budget owner — Run_State has no economy field
evidence:
+// Returns the budget delta (negative = spend, positive = refund) so the caller
+// (Run_State.economy) stays the single owner of the budget.
detail: Run_State carries budget: i32 directly; Economy is a [LATER] layer (ODN-16). The comment references a structure that doesn't exist, misleading the next agent about where the budget invariant lives.
recommended_fix: Say Run_State.budget (or the future Economy seam) in the comment.

title: The junction-endpoint triage lookup ('a first' rule) is copied verbatim into both flow.advance and snapshot_write
detail: The same block appears in advance() (pipe_a[pi]) and near-verbatim as the lb check in pick_pipe. The a-first precedence is a load-bearing rule; three copies invite drift (a future junction-junction change must find all three).
recommended_fix: Extract a single junction_triage_of(t, pipe_slot) helper in core.
